steps.observation: You have 300 seconds. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
# The Last Light

Old Martin had kept the light burning for thirty-one years.

Every evening at dusk, he climbed the spiral staircase — eighty-seven steps, he knew them like his own heartbeat — and lit the lamp. Every morning at dawn, he climbed back up and put it out.

The island gave him fish, rain, and silence. He gave the island purpose.

In October, a letter arrived on the supply boat. *Automated systems will replace all remaining staffed lighthouses by January 1st.* Martin read it twice, folded it carefully, and set it on the kitchen table beneath a stone.

He kept climbing the stairs.

Ships still passed. Tankers mostly, slow dark shapes against the horizon. He wondered if their crews ever looked toward shore and noticed the light, or if it was just data now — a blinking coordinate on a glowing screen.

On his last night, a storm came in hard from the northwest. Martin climbed the stairs and lit the lamp the way he always had, by hand, watching the flame catch and grow and throw itself against the glass. The beam swept out across the black water in long, slow rotations.

Somewhere out there, he told himself, someone is finding their way home.

He sat in the chair by the window and watched until morning.

That was enough.
